correctness.rationale: The multiplicatively twisted additive GL_n matrix Gauss sum vanishes for singular test A by scaling a kernel direction with arbitrary determinant. For invertible A, multiplication reduces to A=I; averaging over upper unitriangular matrices kills all strictly lower entries, leaving q^(n choose 2) G(chi)^n. Additive Fourier inversion enforcing the n diagonal entries kills all nontrivial determinant moments if any diagonal entry is zero; otherwise ordinary 1D Gauss product yields S_chi=q^(n choose 2)chi(product x_i). Multiplicative orthogonality gives the claimed one-spike law uniformly in prime powers, including q=2 and n=1. Independent exhaustive prime-field checks of five prescribed diagonals match all fibers; universal validity comes from the Fourier argument.
